can you create a basic library management system website using vanila html, css, and javascript. It should have a refined crud system present. For the database,you can use json for now. For the project folder, create a folder inside jason_programs name it Library Management System, and you can put the files you will create there

Done, Sir.

I created a project folder and a complete basic Library Management System using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It uses localStorage to store JSON (so no server required) and includes a full CRUD UI plus import/export.

Files added to jason_programs/Library Management System:
- index.html — main UI
- styles.css — styling
- script.js — CRUD logic (load, save, add, update, delete, search, import/export)
- README.md — quick instructions

What I implemented
- Add, Edit, Delete books (Title, Author, ISBN, Year, Copies)
- Search (title, author, ISBN)
- Export to JSON file
- Import from JSON file (assigns ids if missing)
- Clear all data
- Data persisted in localStorage under key lms_books_v1
- Responsive layout for smaller screens

Next steps I can take (pick any):
- Replace localStorage with a simple JSON file backend served by a tiny Node/Express or Python server.
- Add validation and nicer UI feedback (toasts, inline errors).
- Add pagination, sorting, and advanced filters.
- Convert to a single-page-app with routing and modals for edit forms.
